old.name: Varvakios Central Market
old.teaser: Europe's biggest fresh-fish hall — five to ten tonnes a day under an 1886 iron roof.
old.text: Built 1876–1886, paid for by the bequest of Ioannis Varvakis, the Psara-born caviar magnate of the Caspian; the name comes from the Varvakeion Lyceum his money endowed. Come 05:30–08:30 for the fish-hall theatre — shaved ice, silver sardine drifts, auction-pitch voices under iron arches. In the meat market the Epirus canteen feeds butchers around the clock on Fridays and Saturdays, October to Easter. Cash still king, wet floors, closed shoes; the fruit-and-vegetable annex sits across Athinas.
old.meta: WHERE Athinas 42, historic centre · HOURS Mon–Sat 08:00–18:00, fish hall from dawn · PRICE free to wander; fish by weight

old.name: Kallidromiou Saturday Laiki
old.teaser: One graffiti-walled Exarcheia street of Attica smallholders — Marathon lettuces to Megara eggs.
old.text: Athens' liveliest laiki runs along Kallidromiou beneath Strefi Hill. Greek press reports the Financial Times ranked it among the world's great markets, but the detail propre au lieu is in the sellers — egg-man Angelos Koursos, fifty-year veteran Vasilis Makoudakis — trading under the graffiti while a café opens at 05:30 just for the stallholders. Producer prices by the kilo, sharpest in the last hour after 13:30; cash only, bring bags, strictly seasonal.
old.meta: WHERE Kallidromiou St, Exarcheia · HOURS Saturdays only, ~07:00–15:00 · PRICE producer prices by the kilo

gastronomy:Mokka Specialty Coffee.group: The coffee, the resin and the cured meat

old.name: Mokka Specialty Coffee
old.teaser: A kafekopteio perfuming Athinas 44 since 1922 — hot-sand Greek coffee to specialty micro-lots.
old.text: A coffee-roasting shop has stood at Athinas 44, facing the Varvakios block, since 1922 — opened by the Asia Minor refugee Christos Samourkas. Its keeper Nikos Psomas is fourth-generation, from the family that made 'Turkish' coffee officially 'Greek' with the BRAVO brand in the 1960s, and the first Greek juror on the Cup of Excellence; the mezzanine archive tells that story over the roasters. Order the hovoli — Greek coffee buried in hot sand, rising slow, crema-capped — and the beans ground to your brew.
old.meta: WHERE Athinas 44 · HOURS Mon–Sat, market rhythm · PRICE coffee + beans by the bag

gastronomy:Mastihashop.group: The coffee, the resin and the cured meat

old.name: Mastihashop
old.teaser: The Chios growers' own Athens counter — PDO mastiha, raw tears to liqueur.
old.text: Only the mastichochoria of southern Chios can make the lentisk tree 'weep' commercially — a know-how UNESCO inscribed on its Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2014. The growers' association, founded 1938, created mastihashop in 2002 to sell the PDO resin itself, the profits routed back to the mastic villages; the Panepistimiou corner is its Athens counter. Raw tears with a pine-cool crunch that turns to chewing resin and a cathedral-incense perfume; the liqueur and sweets pack small, but mind the cabin liquid rules.
old.meta: WHERE Panepistimiou 6 & Kriezotou · HOURS Mon–Sat · PRICE tears to gift-tier

gastronomy:Miran.group: The coffee, the resin and the cured meat

old.name: Miran
old.teaser: The 1922 Armenian house that brought pastourma to Athens, still curing at Evripidou 45.
old.text: The narrow Evripidou 45 doorway has sold pastourma since 1922, and it is now the visible tip of the largest cured-meat house of its kind in the EU: the grandsons cut to order out front while a 1,300 m² works behind feeds the trade. A genocide survivor from Kayseri opened here in three square metres; the factory left the back room only in 1983. Hand-cut beef under a rust-red cemen crust — fenugreek, garlic, paprika — cellar-cured to a deep funk; vacuum-packs survive a week in a galley fridge.
old.meta: WHERE Evripidou 45 · HOURS Mon–Sat; closed Sun · PRICE pastourma by weight

gastronomy:Bahar.group: The spice row & the sweet houses

old.name: Bahar
old.teaser: Athens' definitive spice house since 1940 — 2,500 references, the trade's worst-kept secret.
old.text: Antonis Manolessos left Santorini for Athens and opened at Evripidou 31 in 1940, on the eve of the war; his son Matthaios has kept the counter since 1976. Eighty-plus years on, the same doorway is the reason the whole spice row smells the way it does — Krokos Kozanis saffron, wild oregano, mountain tea weighed into paper bags off old scales. This Is Athens calls it 'beloved of local chefs and food writers'; the queue into the street proves it daily. Go in with a list.
old.meta: WHERE Evripidou 31 · HOURS Mon–Sat; closed Sun · PRICE spices by the 50 g scoop

gastronomy:Aristokratikon.group: The spice row & the sweet houses

old.name: Aristokratikon
old.teaser: Athens' oldest chocolatier, 1928 — whole Aegina pistachios drowned in dark couverture.
old.text: Panagiotis Karras came down from Epirus in 1928 to 'invest his business demon in a chocolate dream'; five generations on, the house still makes everything by hand to his rules. It fed Maria Callas her praline habit and shipped Turkish delights to Jackie Kennedy — but the point stays Greek: whole Aegina pistachios drowned in dark couverture, Skopelos prunes, Pelion chestnuts. It moved — the city shop is now at Voulis 7, a step off Syntagma; fine chocolate travels badly in an Athens August, buy it in the cool months.
old.meta: WHERE Voulis 7, off Syntagma · HOURS Mon–Sat; closed Sun · PRICE by the piece; boxes in the tens

gastronomy:Krinos.group: The spice row & the sweet houses

old.name: Krinos
old.teaser: The loukoumas benchmark since 1923 — the trypio ring fried to order, honey-syruped.
old.text: The Aiolou 87 address began as the pharmacy of Stamatis Krinos in the mid-1800s; in 1923 Minas Kasimatis of Constantinople turned it into a pastry house, and a century on Athenians still call the doughnut-with-a-hole by the pharmacist's name. Crackling rings, molten centres, honey syrup pooling, cinnamon falling like dust — cash-wise, mosaic-and-formica time travel rather than brunch styling, a short walk from the Varvakios.
old.meta: WHERE Aiolou 87 · HOURS Mon–Sat, daytime; closed Sun · PRICE pocket change

old.name: Domaine Papagiannakos
old.teaser: Old-vines Savatiano and new-wave retsina — Greece's first bioclimatic winery, 35 km east.
old.text: The Mesogeia plain was ancient Athens' vineyard, and Savatiano its workhorse — long scorned as the grape of bad retsina. Three generations argued otherwise (the family has bottled since 1919): Vassilis Papagiannakos built Greece's first bioclimatic, gravity-fed winery in 2007 and pours the Savatiano masterclass that turned sommeliers back toward Attica's own variety — 50-to-60-year-old dry-farmed vines, baked-apple flesh, fresh almond, thyme-scrub salinity. At Markopoulo Mesogaia, about 35 km out toward Porto Rafti; half an hour from the Riviera.
old.meta: WHERE Markopoulo Mesogaia, ~35 km east · HOURS shop Mon–Sat; tastings by appointment · PRICE cellar-door + booked tastings

old.name: Aegina Pistachio Growers' Co-op
old.teaser: Fistiki Aeginis at source — the 1947 co-op handling roughly a third of the island's PDO crop.
old.text: Pistacia vera took to waterless Aegina's volcanic soil better than anywhere in Greece, and in 1996 Brussels sealed 'Fistiki Aeginis' as a PDO — the country's most famous nut. The growers' co-op, founded 1947, opened its harbourfront outlet in 1979; roughly half the island's growers are members. Closed shell, rose-tinged skin, no dye, no excess salt — the safest address for the real thing. Beware the lookalike 'Aegina-style' nuts sold elsewhere; the island itself now lives in the separate Piraeus & Saronic guide.
old.meta: WHERE Aegina town harbourfront · HOURS shop hours · PRICE PDO by the half-kilo
